patterns: Ultra-short runtime (5 to 20 seconds) focusing on one hyper-specific daily psychological habit
Self-deprecating humor framing overthinking or social awkwardness as a shared experience
High visual polish or expressive character animation during mundane internal monologues
Contrasting absurd worst-case scenario thinking with completely normal external reality
Direct validation of intrusive 3 AM thoughts, late-night cringe memories, or boundary issues
title_formulas: POV: You Tried To Stop [Psychological Habit] [Emoji]
opening_3s: Mia freezes mid-sentence while Leo's internal thought bubble explodes into chaotic spirals
Leo makes eye contact with a random object while his brain plays an embarrassing memory from 2018
Mia gives an overly serious step-by-step warning for a completely minor social interaction
comment_themes: Appreciation for smooth, fluid character animation and expressive art styles
Relief at realizing they are not the only ones experiencing niche mental loops
Nostalgia triggered by relatable sound bites or early-2000s life references
Requests for tactics on how to actually quiet their mind during overthinking spirals
avoid: Long-form lectures over 30 seconds that lack a quick comedic punchline
Generic motivational quotes that ignore the realistic frustration of mental loops
Abstract advice without visual cues of Leo and Mia physically reacting
try_next: A 7-second skit where Mia tries to fall asleep, but Leo acts out a cringe memory from middle school inside her thought bubble.
A 12-second skit on 'Social Battery Drain,' showing Leo's energy meter dropping from 100% to 0% after one small talk greeting.
A 15-second visual breakdown of 'Decision Paralysis' as Mia overanalyzes picking a single menu item while Leo waits in horror.
